checkpoint_review: The Router was rigorous and correct in its checkpoint verdicts. The most critical failure is the geometric mismatch: the taxonomy defines a 'loupe' as a 'small circular optical device', whereas the image depicts a rectangular, slide-out style viewer (often called a linen tester or patch magnifier). While functionally similar, it fails the strict morphological definition of the class label provided. The Router correctly marked 'circular shape', 'cylindrical body', 'convex lens', and 'clear glass' as missing/false. The only checkpoints passed were generic material presence and the broad category of 'optical device'. The Router did not skip any testable checkpoints unjustifiably.

I agree with the severities.
